reports.about: In-district, Lunenburg spent $2,103 a pupil less than Ayer Shirley, the middle of the six this project chose.

reports.title: Facilities and grounds
reports.about: Facilities and grounds were voted $1,022,711 for FY2025 and grew 7.5% a year.

reports.title: Employee benefits
reports.about: Employee benefits grew 12.7% a year, the most dollars past the cap of any group; group health is 71% of it.

reports.title: Destination districts
reports.about: 145 of the 177 children schooled elsewhere in FY2026 went to districts that spend more a pupil.

reports.title: Debt service
reports.about: Debt service fell from $4,497,723 to $2,941,322, FY2023 to FY2025, the only one of the twelve groups to fall.

reports.title: Cuts against state counts
reports.about: Of 60 adopted school cuts, 48 name a job no series counts; of the other 12, the state’s count fell with 6.

reports.title: Computer science
reports.about: In 11 school years holding grades 9–12, Lunenburg High recorded 1 computer science section.

reports.title: Comparison districts
reports.about: Of six districts this project chose to compare, Lunenburg spent the least a pupil in FY2025.

reports.title: Budgets without headcounts
reports.about: 6 of the 12 budget groups have a published staff count behind them; one department with a budget has none.

reports.title: Budget by department
reports.about: Schools are 57.1% of the $44,024,349 Town Meeting voted for FY2025; the next three groups together are 27.0%.

reports.title: Average teacher salary
reports.about: Lunenburg’s average teacher salary was $97,233 in FY2025, 2nd of the six districts this project compares.

reports.title: Announced cuts
reports.about: The district named 158 reductions in 9 budget documents across 5 cycles; none records what became of a post.

reports.title: AP subjects
reports.about: 117 of 154 AP exams in SY2025 were English or history; science and math were 31.

reports.title: AP scores
reports.about: 88.3% of AP tests scored 3 or better in SY2025, the highest of 19 years; the lowest was 62.1% in SY2009.

reports.title: AP participation
reports.about: 89 students sat at least one AP exam in SY2025, 154 sittings between them; the count peaked at 122 in SY2018.

reports.title: Total state aid
reports.about: The state’s cherry sheet carries $11,244,422 for Lunenburg for FY2026; Chapter 70 is 82.1% of it.

reports.title: Teachers per pupil
reports.about: Lunenburg had 6.70 teacher FTE per hundred pupils in FY2025, 12th of 13 on the state’s sheet.

reports.title: Teachers over time
reports.about: The state counted 103.4 teacher FTE in FY2026, 10.6 fewer than in FY2024; 95 of 171 year pairs end lower.

reports.title: Teachers by subject
reports.about: From FY2024 to FY2026 subjects lost 12.3 teacher FTE and gained 2.2; science alone fell 4.2.

reports.title: Teachers by school
reports.about: Turkey Hill Elementary went from 27.0 to 18.4 teacher FTE, FY2017 to FY2026; the district fell 8.7.

reports.title: Support staff
reports.about: The town printed 7 counsellors, 3 psychologists and 2 social workers on its FY2025 school rosters.

reports.title: Students and schools
reports.about: 1,568 children were in Lunenburg’s schools in FY2026, near where the count has sat since FY2015. Another 177 residents were schooled in other public districts, 97 of them at Monty Tech.

reports.title: State aid growth
reports.about: Our projection grows all state aid 2.71% a year; the cherry sheet’s median yearly rise was 2.80%.

reports.title: Staff retention
reports.about: The state reports 58.3% of paraprofessionals retained in FY2022 and 66.1% in FY2023, against 93.0% in FY2021.

reports.title: Staff by programme
reports.about: Paraprofessional FTE coded to special education fell from 44.0 to 20.0 while the all-programmes count rose.

reports.title: Spending against the median
reports.about: In FY2024 Lunenburg ranked 238 of 362 districts on spending against its minimum; in FY2018 it was 181 of 361.

reports.title: Share of the school budget
reports.about: Chapter 70 was 35.1% of the FY2026 school appropriation; the School Committee said 35%.

reports.title: School staff
reports.about: The state counted 103.4 teacher FTE in FY2026; whether that is a rise or a fall depends on the year it is measured from. Paraprofessional FTE was 67.0 in FY2025, the most per pupil on the state’s sheet. Nothing published says which posts were filled.

reports.title: School choice flows
reports.about: 58 residents left under school choice in FY2026 and 11 arrived; arrivals were 44 in FY2014.

reports.title: Required local contribution
reports.about: What the state requires the town to put in rose 37.8% from FY2019 to FY2026; Chapter 70 rose 22.4%.

reports.title: Printed school rosters
reports.about: The town printed 250 names on its school rosters in FY2025, against 194 in FY2011.

reports.title: People and posts
reports.about: The state counted 123 teachers in FY2023, holding 112.8 full-time equivalent posts between them.

reports.title: Paraprofessionals over time
reports.about: The state counted 67.0 paraprofessional FTE in FY2025, against 14.8 in FY2013 and 46.4 in FY2009.

reports.title: Paraprofessional counts compared
reports.about: For FY2025 the state counts 67.0 paraprofessional FTE; the town printed 52 paraprofessional names.

reports.title: Net school spending
reports.about: Lunenburg spent 116.0% of the state’s minimum in FY2024, and met the minimum in all 31 years.

reports.title: Nearby district enrolment
reports.about: Lunenburg’s enrolment fell 14.0% from FY2008 to FY2026; 3 of 4 nearby districts fell further.

reports.title: Monty Tech enrolment
reports.about: Monty Tech enrolled 1,403 pupils in FY2026 from 18 member towns; 97 were Lunenburg residents.

reports.title: Monty Tech assessment
reports.about: Lunenburg’s FY2026 Monty Tech bill was $1,334,521; 95.2% of it is a minimum the state sets.

reports.title: Minimum aid
reports.about: All of FY2026’s $240,450 increase was the Legislature’s minimum: $150 for each of 1,603 pupils.

reports.title: Leaving and arriving
reports.about: DESE’s rates imply about 90 children leave each year; enrolment fell 171 in 17 years.

reports.title: High-needs students
reports.about: English learners went from 3 to 70; low income was measured three ways and is not one series.

reports.title: Grade-to-grade loss
reports.about: On average 20.5% of eighth graders do not return for grade 9; other grades lose 3.0% to 6.4%.

reports.title: Grade 8 loss trend
reports.about: The latest grade 8 rate, 27.7%, is the second-highest of 17 years, inside a range the town has always been in.

reports.title: Foundation budget
reports.about: The state priced Lunenburg’s schools at $22,073,946 for FY2026; Chapter 70 equals 41.8% of that.

reports.title: Enrolment by year
reports.about: 1,568 children in FY2026: 321 fewer than the FY2001 peak, and close to where the count has sat since FY2015.

reports.title: Enrolment by grade band
reports.about: Grades 9–12 lost 30.0% of their children from FY2008 to FY2026; pre-K to grade 5 lost 5.8%.

reports.title: District staff directory
reports.about: The district’s staff directory listed 257 people on 30 October 2026; it carries no FTE and no fund.

reports.title: Departure scenario
reports.about: A scenario on assumed rates: 78 students choosing out would take $401,700 from the town in year one.

reports.title: Children schooled elsewhere
reports.about: 177 resident children were in other public districts in FY2026, against 186 in FY2014; the mix changed.

reports.title: Cherry sheet variance
reports.about: Cherry sheet receipts came in $390,814 short of the estimate in 2024 and $327,281 over in 2023.

reports.title: Cherry sheet assessments
reports.about: The cherry sheet charged Lunenburg $1,003,251 for FY2026; 80.3% was tuition for pupils schooled elsewhere.

reports.title: Chapter 70 by year
reports.about: Chapter 70 was $9,229,410 in FY2026 and $3,921,700 in FY2007; it fell in 2 of 19 years.

reports.title: Chapter 70 aid
reports.about: Chapter 70 was $9,229,410 of the $11,244,422 the state’s cherry sheet gave Lunenburg for FY2026. All of that year’s rise was the Legislature’s $150-a-pupil minimum; the formula itself added $0.

reports.title: Aid per pupil
reports.about: Chapter 70 averaged $5,757.59 a pupil in FY2026, yet one pupil more or fewer moved it by $150.00.

reports.title: Year-end transfers
reports.about: Transfers moved $394,929 into school accounts and $309,839 out; the department ended $85,090 up, net.

reports.title: Who may spend it
reports.about: Only the general fund, $3,147,179 of $9,061,421, may go to any lawful use, by a two-thirds vote.

reports.title: Tuition budget
reports.about: FY2027 budgets out-of-district tuition at $700,142, $591,151 below FY2026, a 46% cut.

reports.title: Tuition at year end
reports.about: FY2027 budgets $700,142 for the two tuition lines on which FY2026 spent $1,202,771.

reports.title: Town unspent balance
reports.about: In June, before the close, town departments stood $858,462 under a $27,647,670 budget.

reports.title: Surplus by category
reports.about: Accounts under budget left $1,683,552 and accounts over used $1,201,434 of it; the net is $482,118.

reports.title: Students with an IEP
reports.about: 258 Lunenburg children had a special education plan in FY2026, 16.3% of those enrolled.

reports.title: Stabilization withdrawals
reports.about: The record shows $317,392 taken from stabilization funds in 9 votes, none from the general fund.

reports.title: Stabilization funds
reports.about: The town holds $9,061,421 in nine stabilization accounts as of 1 July 2025. Only the general fund’s $3,147,179 may be spent on anything lawful.

reports.title: Stabilization fund balances
reports.about: The town’s ledger files $9,061,421 under its nine stabilization accounts, at the start of FY2026.

reports.title: Stabilization deposits
reports.about: Town Meeting put $350,000 into the two town funds in May 2024, and passed over both articles in May 2025.

reports.title: Special education overruns
reports.about: A special education line ran over its vote in 13 of 17 years; the worst, FY2013, by $223,774.

reports.title: Special education costs
reports.about: Out-of-district tuition was $1,205,949 in FY2025, and 39.3% of it was paid outside the general fund. The state repaid $579,142 in FY2026 through the circuit breaker, a year after the costs.

reports.title: Snow and Reserve Fund
reports.about: Snow removal paid $1,038,092 against $355,571 voted; the $185,000 Reserve Fund paid nothing.

reports.title: School retiree insurance
reports.about: An account named for school retiree health paid $1,262,376 from the town’s insurance department.

reports.title: Reserves against the gap
reports.about: Spent on the school gap, the general fund covers FY2028 and FY2029 and runs out in FY2030, by our arithmetic.

reports.title: Psychologist line
reports.about: One of four school psychologist accounts, $98,784 budgeted, paid nothing in FY2026.

reports.title: Paraprofessional overrun
reports.about: Paraprofessional accounts ran $208,082 over in FY2026; $99,064 of it was paid against no budget.

reports.title: Out-of-district tuition
reports.about: $1,205,949 went to out-of-district tuition in FY2025; 39.3% of it was paid outside the general fund.

reports.title: Out-of-district placements
reports.about: The town counted 10 children placed out of district in FY2025, against 30 in FY2015.

reports.title: In-district special education
reports.about: The paraprofessional budget line grew 12.78% a year over 10 budgets; the state’s FTE fell 63.3%.

reports.title: Hiring versus placing
reports.about: Placements fell while in-district budgets rose; nothing published shows one caused the other.

reports.title: General stabilization fund
reports.about: The general fund’s cash rose every year from FY2012 to FY2025, to $3,147,179.

reports.title: Free cash sources
reports.about: Two thirds of the free cash identified in July 2025, $2,457,761, was money appropriated and not spent.

reports.title: Free cash guideline
reports.about: Free cash is 6.65% of the budget, inside the 5% to 7% the Town cites; 7 of the last 10 years fell short.

reports.title: Free cash for schools
reports.about: Kept above the 5% floor, $794,872 could be redirected, $137,792 short of the FY2028 gap (our arithmetic).

reports.title: Free cash balance
reports.about: The state certified $3,354,370 of free cash as of 1 July 2025, the most in any year the Town’s records list.

reports.title: Free cash and capital
reports.about: Free cash paid $655,424 of the $1,225,000 FY2026 capital programme; FY2027 plans $991,627 of $1,830,203.

reports.title: FY2026 year end
reports.about: The school general fund ended FY2026 with $482,118 unspent, 1.8% of its budget, counting orders still owed. Counted the same way, FY2025 left $554,945. Town departments stood $858,462 under in June.

reports.title: Cost per placement
reports.about: No published document says what one out-of-district placement costs.

reports.title: Class size limits
reports.about: A separate special education group may hold 8 students to one educator, or 12 with an aide.

reports.title: Circuit breaker account
reports.about: The account closed FY2026 at $281,806, down from $482,004 at the close of FY2020.

reports.title: Circuit breaker
reports.about: The one state payment that moves when a child is placed: part of the cost, a year late, already in the vote.

reports.title: Town budget and fee fund
reports.about: The fee fund paid 45.8% of athletics spending in FY2024 and 5.7% in FY2025, on the town’s books.

reports.title: Total athletics cost
reports.about: No document states one total: three sheets give $185,356 to $349,145 for the same teams in FY2024.

reports.title: State reimbursement
reports.about: The state repays 5.5% of what the town spends on buses, all of it for special education.

reports.title: Spending by category
reports.about: Coaches and buses cost most on the district’s sheet; the town’s officials account held $0 in FY2026.

reports.title: Special education transportation
reports.about: The fastest-growing bus line: 10.1% a year, and $67,555 past its FY2026 budget.

reports.title: School bus costs
reports.about: Buses are getting more expensive, in special education and in the regular-route contract. The state repays only a slice of special education busing. The athletic line rose because the district moved that cost from player fees to the town budget, mostly taxes.

reports.title: Participation
reports.about: The district counted 649 sport participations in FY2026, against 675 in FY2024.

reports.title: FY2027 bus budget
reports.about: School-day buses rise 11.2% in FY2027; the total shows 2.4% because athletic buses were cut.

reports.title: FY2027 athletic bus cut
reports.about: FY2027 cut athletic buses from the town budget, then put $60,000 back, most on the fee fund.

reports.title: FY2026 athletics underspend
reports.about: Athletics closed FY2026 with $55,300 of its $518,334 town budget unspent, on the town’s ledger.

reports.title: Dee Bus contract
reports.about: Regular routes cost exactly the contract price, which is fixed through FY2028.

reports.title: Cost per sport
reports.about: Not one of 25 teams carries the same FY2024 cost in all three district sheets.

reports.title: Bus fee
reports.about: The new bus fee did not lower what the school budget paid for buses in FY2026.

reports.title: Bus cost by sport
reports.about: Track costs most on the district’s sheet: $13,864 in FY2024, ahead of the next sport’s $9,078.

reports.title: Away trips by sport
reports.about: The posted schedules list 240 away games in FY2026, about 176 bus trips by our estimate.

reports.title: Athletics costs
reports.about: Athletics is paid from two pots, the town budget and a fee fund. The town’s ledger shows $463,034 spent in FY2026 and the fee fund $146,911; the district’s own sheets disagree on what each team costs, by a multiple.

reports.title: Athletic fee
reports.about: The high school fee for a first child, a season, went from $250 in FY2025 to $325 in FY2026.

reports.title: Athletic bus funding
reports.about: From FY2025, athletic buses moved from player fees to the town budget, mostly taxes.

reports.title: The annual town reports
reports.about: Every annual town report, 1959 to FY2025, each one downloadable with the sha256 of the bytes we hold — and what we read out of them, by category. Says plainly which pages tie to a total the page itself prints, and why the rest cannot be checked from the page.

reports.title: Towns like us: what they pay, what they spend
reports.about: How Lunenburg compares with the towns it borders, the peers this project chose, and the towns most like it across the whole state, on what a town is and what it does — with a map of every town in Massachusetts.

reports.title: What the town is deciding now
reports.about: What the town is deciding now

reports.title: The School Committee’s finances — every fund and line it owns
reports.about: The School Committee’s finances, every line: the appropriation, its revolving funds, grants, gifts and trusts, with what each held at 31 March 2026 and what it has done since FY2011 — the first of a page per board and department, from a registry of every accounting measure the town prints.

reports.title: The budget feed — every board, everything about money
reports.about: What every board is doing to prepare for Town Meeting: the omnibus budget, the school budget above all, and the warrant. What is coming, where this cycle stands, what was said most recently, what was posted. Not every mention of money — the budget being built, and what will land on the warrant.

reports.title: The boards — each one, in one place
reports.about: Every board and committee the town posts for, one page each: what is coming, what happened, every vote we have minutes for, where the board’s time goes, and when budget season has fallen on its agendas in past years.

reports.title: This week in town — meetings coming up, minutes and recordings just posted
reports.about: Meetings coming up for the Select Board, Finance Committee and School Committee with what is on each agenda, minutes just posted, recordings just published, and what happened at the last recorded meetings. Refreshed daily.

reports.title: The blog — one finding at a time, in two minutes
reports.about: Every finding this project has published as a post: the figures, what it means for a resident, a Finance Committee member and a School Committee member, and the links to the report underneath it. About two minutes each.

reports.title: Meeting minutes — written from the recordings
reports.about: Our minutes of recorded meetings, written from the captions: votes, transfers, budget items, decisions and public comment, every item linked to the video at that second, and checked against the town’s minutes where they exist.

reports.title: What a family actually pays
reports.about: Every school fee a Lunenburg household can be charged, priced for one to four children, and the three places the published record runs out.

reports.title: If students leave — what school choice would cost
reports.about: What it would cost the town if more children left under school choice — a scenario with dials, priced against DESE’s own counts.

reports.title: What you can ask this archive
reports.about: Every question this archive can answer, in plain English and without a line of SQL. The list a resident should start from: pick the question you actually have and follow it to the figure and the document behind it.

reports.title: A hundred questions this archive can answer
reports.about: The same questions with the query that answers each one, run against the database on every build — so none of them is a claim about what this data can do. If one stops answering, the build fails.

reports.title: Connecting the school budget to the Town's books
reports.about: What can be followed from the school budget to the town’s books, and where it stops. Two levels join, the third cannot, and the format a report arrives in decides which.
